To understand how a computer reads data from a Solid-State Drive (SSD), it is essential to first recognize that an SSD is fundamentally different from a traditional Hard Disk Drive (HDD). While an HDD uses spinning magnetic platters and a moving read/write head, an SSD is a purely electronic storage device with no moving parts.
